In question 13 of the Quiz 1 Mock for System Commands, the question asks:

Which of the following commands will create a directory projects with a subdirectory 2024 , then create a symbolic link named current pointing to 2024 , and finally verify the link?

The accepted answers are :

incorrect_options1568×536 72.8 KB

However, these options end up creating broken links (red in colour).

This option worked correctly :

correct_option956×228 29.8 KB

Please correct me if I’m wrong or I’m missing something here.

link_counts.title: BPT1 showing "Absent" despite completing it on VM

posts.name: Girish
posts.cooked:
Hi @23f2004275 , in the option you have mentioned that worked correctly, you are creating the current link inside the projects directory for the 2024 dir in you current directory, I believe the structure expected is
–Base folder (You are here)
------ project
---------- 2024
---------- current

So the target for the ln command is project/2024 and it cannot be 2024

Please correct me if I am wrong here

posts.name: Wasim
posts.cooked: projects/2024 will end up creating a broken link because it checks for 2024 from the parent directory of ‘current’ which is projects, and ends up looking at projects/projects/2024 where nothing exists. The right answer is ln -s 2024 projects/current if you don’t want a broken link.

posts.name: Girish
posts.cooked:
projects/2024 will check for 2024 under projects right? (Correct, parent directory of current, which has projects and inside that 2024, so, it will end up looking correctly for projects/2024
@23f2004275

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked: Wasim is correct. Soft links store the path. And it should be given path relative to itself, not pwd. So only 2024 should be given.
